newsitem.title: JAPAN: PRESS DIGEST - Top Japan business news - Dec 19.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Top Japan business news - Dec 19.

text.p: Kirin Brewery Co Ltd and Sapporo Breweries Ltd plan to provide beer list prices excluding the consumption tax when the tax rate is raised from three to five percent in April 1997. Under the current system, tax is included in the list price.
Asahi Breweries Ltd is considering following suit.

Mazda Motor Corp plans to remodel its Capella station wagon to incorporate a compact direct fuel injection diesel engine from October 1997. This will be the first Japanese model equipped with the engine. Isuzu Motors Ltd and Nissan Motor Co Ltd are expected to follow suit.

All Nippon Airways Co Ltd plans to start an air ticket sales and reservation service for Burma's Air Mandalay as early as February. ANA hopes to raise the seat occupancy rates on its Osaka-Yangon route from the present 50 percent by linking up with Air Mandalay's domestic and international network.

Four environment-related equipment manufacturers are expected to post record current profits in the year to March 1997. Ebara Corp expects to mark its 11th consecutive year of record profit, and Kurita Water Industries Ltd its ninth consecutive record year.

Four leading discount chains for men's clothing are expected to see sales and pre-tax profit increases in the year to March 1997. Although sales at their conventional men's apparel stores remain sluggish, their casual clothing outlets are doing brisk business.
Five medium-sized printing companies are expected to increase their pre-tax profit in the year to March 1997, helped by an increase in commercial printing orders and production streamlining.

Nippon Kayaku Co Ltd is expected to have increased its pre-tax profit by 35 percent to more than five billion yen for the first half year to November 1996 from the same period a year earlier, helped by strong sales of profitable medicines and cuts in development costs.

Two pharmaceutical companies, Banyu Pharmaceutical Co Ltd and Yoshitomi Pharmaceutical Industries Ltd, are expected to mark record current profits in the year to March 1997, while two other drug makers, Ono Pharmaceuticals Co Ltd and Dainippon Pharmaceutical Co Ltd, are likely to see earnings fall.
